derivation: STANDARDS-DERIVED. Every field traces to a standard, a regulation or a recognised industry body per campaign/SOURCE_AUTHORITY_PACK.md. Citation statuses observe source_status_ceiling. Field service management is not a standards domain; where the pack says so, the field is judgment.
taxonomy_origin: TAXONOMY ORIGIN, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT FACT FROM THE DERIVATION ABOVE. The derivation line describes where FIELD CONTENT comes from: every field value traces to a standard, a regulation or a recognised industry body and carries its citation. It does NOT describe where the taxonomy comes from. Which processes exist, how they are grouped and what they are called is a practitioner synthesis of delivered implementations, generalised until it is product- and client-neutral. Of the 102 process groups, 43 originate in programme material, 28 in domain research, 20 in a published source and 11 in folder and file names; the provenance layer grades every one and names what to read next. This model is DELIVERED PRACTICE SPECIFIED AGAINST STANDARDS, not a standard turned into a model - and saying so is not a weakness. A taxonomy proven in delivery and then held against the standards is a stronger claim than one derived from a standard and never built.
field_set: EN 17007:2017 cl. 5.2 maintenance process profile, corroborated by ISO 9001:2015 cl. 4.4.1 a) to h).
gaps: FSM is not a standards domain. IEC 61968-6 standardises ServiceOrder exchange, not how 10.2 is scheduled, dispatched or executed. ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018 is cited only as a labelled ITSM analogue for intake (8.6.2) and service level (8.3.3), never for scheduling, dispatch or execution.

There is no federal nonpay-disconnection or winter/medical-protection code for distribution customers. The pack lists no customer-protection statute (no HEFPA, no 52 Pa. Code Chapter 56, no CPUC D.12-03-054). 10.4.4 is therefore state PUC and tariff, named as judgment, with 16 U.S.C. 824o cited only to keep NERC out.
Deposit, doorstep-payment and reconnect-clock rules are tariff. 18 CFR 101 is plant accounting, not a customer-deposit code.
IEEE 1547 (DER interconnection) is not in the pack and is not cited. FERC SGIP is wholesale. 10.6.6/10.6.7 interconnection method is judgment plus 16 U.S.C. 824o and IEC 61968-6 NE.
There is no CIM Customer class in the Work package. 10.1 uses WorkLocation plus CS. IEC 61968-6 is electric-scoped; gas borrows it.
IEC 61968-9:2024 Ed. 3 is cited by title for meter operate. Its body is paywalled and is not paraphrased.

APQC 14.4.2 (pcf_id 19329) Install/remove/energize/re-energize meters sits under metering. This model splits it across 6.3 (endpoint), 10.4/10.5 (operate at the premise) and 10.6.4 (set). APQC 14.3.1 (19308) is the assignment-pack touch on 10.1.

10.2 is a specialised application of 3.4/4.1, not a second scheduler. 10.3.3 is the customer message; 9.0 owns the outage. 10.6.5 commissions the service at the premise; 19.1.3 coordinates energisation of network assets. 10.6.1 classifies; 2.0 designs.

EN 17007 has no customer, deposit, disconnection-protection or interconnection process. COR.1, ACT.*, DOC.6, DTA.1, BUD.3, MAN.5, MRQ.6 and IMP.7 are the closest names and several are stretches, recorded as such.
cl. 4.2 has no document or health-and-safety component. Notices sit on CS, site hazards on CS, clearances on NO.
CGA 3-16 is locate-request content, not a service-order content model. No spanning gas/electric service-order content model exists.

controls.text: Deposit rules are tariff and state. None is in the pack. 18 CFR 101 is plant accounting, not a customer deposit code. The decision is still required before a start.

controls.text: 18 CFR 101 is plant accounting. Contribution-in-aid-of-construction is tariff, not a FERC construction-cost rule. AACE RPs are guidelines, not standards, and are not required here for a service set.

controls.text: IEEE 1547 is the usual interconnection standard and is not in the Source Authority Pack, so it is not cited. FERC SGIP is wholesale. Distribution interconnection rules are state. EN 17007 MRQ.6 is maintenance input to someone else's design, not an interconnection code.
